title: DPD-1.1 — Shared Server Cleanup Evidence
summary: record the implemented exact public cleanup path, Publish exclusion cutover, focused verification, and DPD-1.2 stop gate
content_html:
DPD-1.1 — Shared Server Cleanup Evidence

Result

DPD-1.1 is complete. Confirmed ordinary parent and child document Delete now plans exact current-public impacts, commits the existing canonical and working mutation first, removes only the deleted document projections and affected public inventory references, and requires targeted Catalogue URL follow-through before returning success. Scope and sub-scope lifecycle Delete retain their separate root and configuration ownership while applying the required public follow-through. DPD-1.2 browser work has not started.

Delivered Contract

  • docs_public_delete_cleanup.py owns one focused current-public planner and apply path for ordinary parent and child Delete. Preview adds public_cleanup without writing and reports exact requested identities, projected identity subset, by-ID and owned Mermaid removals, changed public inventory paths, removed public URLs, and affected Catalogue targets.
  • Parent Delete filters the current public tree, Recent, search, and supported document-location payload from the current public snapshot. Child Delete filters only its public manifest, by-ID and owned Mermaid projection, derived locations, and Catalogue URLs. Neither path copies newer working bytes into public output.
  • A deleted report host loses its parent projection and host-derived locations, including child URLs. Surviving child source, manifest, by-ID, Mermaid, configuration, and sibling files are not inferred as host-owned.
  • Local and local-external collections return public_cleanup.applicable: false. Direct and lineage-tracked documents use the same exact identity path; lineage does not participate in cleanup planning.
  • Public-product or Catalogue failure returns non-success with committed: true, retry_delete: false, and the failed public stage. Existing child source restoration remains limited to source and working-rebuild failure.
  • Public lifecycle scope Delete removes its manifest-owned roots and then performs the required Catalogue URL refresh. Sub-scope lifecycle Delete removes its own child roots and applies the exact report-host cleanup after the parent rebuild.
  • Publish now emits docs_publish_gate_v2, excluded, and excluded_count. Its negative plan comes only from current explicit publishable: false roots, descendants, or child entries; unrelated public files and files merely absent from source are retained and unreported. No compatibility removed alias remains.

Focused Verification

  • $HOME/miniconda3/bin/python3 -m pytest -q docs-viewer/tests/python/test_docs_public_delete_cleanup.py docs-viewer/tests/python/test_docs_publish_gate.py docs-viewer/tests/python/test_docs_management_mutations.py docs-viewer/tests/python/test_docs_management_subscope_delete.py docs-viewer/tests/python/test_docs_scope_lifecycle.py docs-viewer/tests/python/test_docs_management_routes.py docs-viewer/tests/python/test_docs_management_publishable.py docs-viewer/tests/python/test_build_document_locations.py docs-viewer/tests/python/test_docs_catalogue_document_urls.py studio/tests/python/test_catalogue_document_url_refresh.py — 117 passed.
  • bin/lint-python across the nine changed Python service and test files — passed.
  • $HOME/miniconda3/bin/python3 -m py_compile across the changed Python service and test files — passed.
  • git diff --check — passed.
  • The focused sensitive-path scan found only the pre-existing deliberate /Users/private redaction fixture and semantic-token path names; no credential or machine-path regression was introduced.

The permanent checks falsify exact parent and child removal, unaffected sibling bytes, report-host child-file retention, owned Mermaid cleanup, local no-op behavior, source-before-public ordering, strict committed Catalogue failure, lifecycle behavior, Publish false-only exclusions, missing-source retention, document locations, and Catalogue URL refresh.

Independent Diff Review

The bounded diff contains one focused cleanup service, integration into existing mutation and lifecycle owners, the Publish response/removal cutover, focused tests, and this evidence. Review confirmed there is no scope-wide Publish call, public rebuild from working bytes, publication inference from source metadata or lineage, shared-media deletion, route-shaped child cascade, missing-source Publish reconciliation, compatibility alias, new Delete control, or generic projection engine. Mermaid enumeration is confined to the configured public projection asset root and exact document-identity pattern.

The existing browser Publish surface still reads removed_count, and existing Delete confirmation/completion copy does not yet present public_cleanup. Those are the explicit DPD-1.2 browser and refresh follow-through seam, not part of DPD-1.1. Stop before DPD-1.2 implementation approval.
